text:
alex: Quick experiment dump — hybrid cohort routing + KV prefetch enabled on canary (g5-16). TL;DR: p95 token latency down ~15-20% for short/med, long tails unchanged, CPU kernel spill sometimes triggers and increases decode jitter. Need ideas on token budgets and admission policy.

maria: Nice. What cohorts did you use? and decode-rate buckets?

alex: Cohorts: short (<64), medium (64-512), long (>512). Decode-rate buckets heuristically split by observed decode speed: fast >200 tok/s, mid 50-200, slow <50. Hybrid routing groups by (prompt_bucket, decode_bucket).

sam: That mapping makes sense. Did you change token_budget per cohort?

alex: Yes — initial mapping: short_fast -> 256, short_mid -> 128, medium_* -> 128, long_* -> 64. The idea was to cap KV prefetch size and avoid over-allocating token budget to long decoders.

alex: Config excerpt:
```yaml
cohort_map:
  - name: short_fast
    prompt_max: 64
    decode_rate: fast
    token_budget: 256
    kv_prefetch: true
  - name: medium_mid
    prompt_min: 64
    prompt_max: 512
    decode_rate: mid
    token_budget: 128
    kv_prefetch: true
  - name: long_slow
    prompt_min: 512
    decode_rate: slow
    token_budget: 64
    kv_prefetch: false
```

alex: Also flipped kernel hints: prefer fused-attn for short sequences, fallback to split kernels when decode_time per step > threshold. That reduced short-case latency but introduced a few kernel spills (memory oversubscribe) on some workloads.

toni: Can you paste the profiler output for the spill cases?

perfbot: profile: canary-2026-03-12 03:14 UTC — job=hybrid-cohort-route, backend=g5-16
  p50_per_token: 5.4ms, p95_per_token: 12.2ms, p99_per_token: 45.1ms
  kv_prefetch_hit_rate: 0.74
  kernel_spills: 7/1200 requests (0.58%)
  spill_source: kernel_memory/alloc_hint_mismatch

alex: The spill pattern: happens when medium prompts with mid decode hit bursty prefix cache misses and we try to prefetch a large KV chunk; combined with fused-attn memory usage it crosses threshold. When spill occurs, decode latency jumps 3-4x for that stream.

maria: Hmm. Maybe lower token_budget for medium_mid when cluster memory pressure high. Also consider prefetch throttling per-GPU based on outstanding prefetched bytes.

sam: Agree. We could also make kv_prefetch conditional on decode_rate bucket: only prefetch for fast decoders where the prefetch amortizes. For slow decoders, prefetch often wastes memory.

alex: Did a quick run: switched medium_mid token_budget 128 -> 96 and made kv_prefetch=false for medium_slow. Results: p95 overall improved 6% and kernel_spills -> 1/1200. Downside: slightly higher p50 for medium_fast (prefetch off).

toni: Any change in throughput or GPU utilization?

alex: GPU util dropped ~3% for canary, but tail latency improved. Throughput steady since we throttle admission when queue exceeds token_budget-based thresholds.

maria: We should add an admission policy tweak: when queue latency > X ms, reduce token_budget globally by 10% and disable kv_prefetch for medium cohort until queue recovers. That buys stability.

sam: Also worth adding a decode-rate smoothing window before assigning decode buckets. Right now jitter causes bucket flapping every few requests which triggers churn in prefetch.

alex: Good call. I used 5s smoothing in a follow-up and bucket flaps dropped 87%. Prefetch churn reduced accordingly.

ci-bot: deploy-notify: rolled canary with token_budget adjustments to us-east-1/g5-16 at 03:40 UTC.

toni: Next steps? I'd like a short experiment matrix: (token_budget variants) x (kv_prefetch on/off) x (decode_smoothing windows). Run 10k requests steady-state per cell, capture kernel_spills, p95 per-token, kv_hit_rate.

maria: I'll own the matrix. Will run on canary cluster and post results by EOD.

alex: Thanks — also add a metric for kernel_hint_switch_count per request so we can correlate hint flips with spills.

sam: And log admission drops due to queue length and token_budget caps.

alex: Great. If anyone sees unexplained p99 spikes, ping me and I'll pull raw traces. :mag:
